title: Hazard Refund Need — Counting the Insurance Premiums by Renewal or by Quarter
content:
In a review of a returned hazard premium on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, the insurance part of the hazard refund need is counted by the number of hazard insurance payments the reserve made within the twelve months before the handling date (payments on the reserve's ledger dated no later than the handling date and fewer than 12 whole calendar months before it).

| Hazard payments from the reserve in those 12 months | Insurance part of the hazard refund need |
|---|---|
| Exactly one | Renewal dates: the annual hazard premium on file counts in full only when the next hazard renewal, one year after the due date of the latest paid hazard insurance bill, is fewer whole months from the handling date than the horizon months; the annual flood premium on file counts in full only when the next flood renewal, one year after the due date of the latest paid flood insurance bill, is fewer whole months away than the horizon months; premiums that count are added together, and a premium with no paid bill of its kind adds nothing |
| Two or more | Quarter blocks: each started quarter of the horizon carries a quarter of the annual hazard and flood premiums on file — the number of started quarters (horizon months divided by three, a fraction counting as a whole quarter) times one quarter of the two premiums together |
| None | Not set by this rule |

The latest paid bill of a kind is the paid bill of that kind with the latest due date. Months to a renewal are whole calendar months from the handling date to the renewal date, below zero where the renewal date has passed.

**Hypothetical figures** (hazard 1,600.00, flood 800.00 on file):
- One payment, horizon 3 months, hazard renewal 2 whole months away, flood renewal 5: insurance part 1,600.00.
- Two payments, horizon 5 months: 2 started quarters times 600.00, which is 1,200.00.
